text: This paper is the mathematical-relativity companion to T5: the geometry of the ascent $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ at the black-hole singularity, in three parts. Part one, where division fails: the Schwarzschild gauge field is a ray in a one-parameter unipotent group, and the curvature factorises exactly, at every radius, into a divergent conformal scale times a fixed shape operator $S$ satisfying $S^2 + S = 2$. Part two, the covariant form: the vacuum field equations are exactly equivalent to the covariant constancy of the null scale section of the rank-six tractor bundle, a parallel ideal point; for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the point leaves the cone with squared norm $\Lambda/3$, and its stabiliser rotates from parabolic Poincar\'e to reductive (anti-)de Sitter. Part three, the approach and the tests: under a blow-up weighted by the Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ the tractor formulation extends to the singular locus for the Einstein velocity-dominated class, with values-level boundary holonomy exactly $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, for $\Lambda = 0$ the Levi factor of the frozen point's parabolic stabiliser, and transport-level convergence along tangential curves of fixed Hubble-normalised length; and Kerr passes three tests: unipotency on a null shear, a complex factorisation locating the ring and leaving the disc regular, and the conformal scale as the inverse cube of the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor. At the perturbed Cauchy horizon point-level structure extends continuously while connection-level structure generically fails, proved in spherical symmetry and expected for Kerr; the conformal-over-metric separation is the sharpest open problem. Eighty-two checks verify the computational identities.

title: Introduction
text:
T5 of this series \cite{ButlerT5} runs a six-step chain from the Schwarzschild gauge field to the Page curve, and at three of its links it defers to a companion geometry paper: for the detailed geometry of where and how division fails, for the covariant meaning of the ascent at the level of the field equations, and for the tests that decide whether the ascended description has physical content or is only a redescription. This is that paper.

The object under study is the gauge-theoretic formulation of general relativity in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$, due to Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite{LDG1998}: gravity as a position-dependent linear map $\hb$ on a flat background, with every metrical statement built from $\hb^{-1}$. The theory's geometric content exists exactly where $\hb$ is invertible, and the series' transport principle \cite{ButlerT1} is a general theory of the loci where it is not. Three questions arise the moment the principle is applied to a black hole, and they organise the paper's three parts.

\emph{Where, exactly, does division fail, and what is the algebraic character of the approach?} Part one (the section ``Part one: where division fails'') answers with two exact factorisations. The Schwarzschild gauge trajectory is a ray in a one-parameter unipotent group: at every radius the field is a finite null-type shear of the identity, and the singularity is the divergence of the shear parameter (Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}). The curvature factorises exactly, at every radius, into a divergent conformal prefactor $-M/r^3$ times a fixed, mass-independent shape operator $S$ satisfying $S^2 + S = 2$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling}): the entire approach to the singularity is carried by a single conformal weight, and what survives the approach is conformal data.

\emph{Is the ascent $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ a property of the equations or something added to them?} Part two (the section ``Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point'') proves the strongest available answer: no limit is needed. The vacuum field equations are exactly equivalent, at every radius, to the covariant constancy of the distinguished null scale section of the rank-six ambient (tractor) bundle: a parallel ideal point of the fibre quadric (Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}). The equations of vacuum gravity are natively a statement in the ascended description, and the familiar metric form is what that statement looks like after a scale is chosen. The cosmological constant enters at theorem level: for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point leaves the cone, its squared norm is $\Lambda/3$, and its stabiliser rotates from the parabolic Poincar\'e group to the reductive de Sitter or anti-de Sitter group (Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}): $\Lambda$ measures precisely the failure of infinity to be parabolic.

\emph{Does the covariant description actually reach the singularity?} Part three answers in two halves. the section ``Part three, first half: the approach'' proves the weighted limit theorem: blowing up the interior along the singular locus with direction-dependent weights equal to the Kasner exponents $(-1/3, 2/3, 2/3)$, the Hubble-normalised connection and the parallel tractor extend continuously to the exceptional boundary, with explicit rates ($O(\tau^{2/3})$ in the boosts, $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotations), and the values-level boundary holonomy algebra is exactly $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, which for $\Lambda = 0$ is the Levi factor of the frozen point's parabolic stabiliser with no component in the nilradical, and for $\Lambda \neq 0$ a proper subalgebra of its reductive stabiliser (Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}). The theorem is proved in full for the Schwarzschild class, extends verbatim to Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Theorem \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}), and carries a sharp delimiter: for generic mixmaster singularities the frame limit provably fails to exist, and the correct generic statement must be billiard-invariant (Remark \claimref{note.interior.generic-delimiter-mixmaster}). the section ``Part three, second half: the Kerr tests'' then runs the Kerr tests: the whole Kerr family is unipotent on a null shear (Proposition \claimref{interior.unipotency-across-kerr-family}); the curvature takes the Schwarzschild form with a complexified scale whose non-invertibility locus is exactly the ring, with the disc interior regular (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring}); the complex scale is the inverse cube of the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor, so the framework's scalar-plus-pseudoscalar scale is a hidden twistorial object (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor}); and at the perturbed Cauchy horizon the imported PDE results establish survival by derivative level, point-level structure (metric and conformal alike) extending continuously while connection-level structure generically fails (proved in spherical symmetry, expected for Kerr), with the strict conformal-over-metric separation registered as the sharpest successor problem (the section ``The perturbed Cauchy horizon'').

title: Prior art
text: Each part of the paper relies on named prior art, and the boundaries are declared here once. \emph{Gauge theory gravity} is due to Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite{LDG1998}, with the textbook treatment in \cite{DoranLasenby2003}; the field equations, the Newtonian (Painlev\'e-Gullstrand) gauge, and the Kerr-Schild forms used below are theirs, and the curvature computations we import are so marked. \emph{Tractor calculus} goes back to Thomas and was formalised by Bailey, Eastwood and Gover \cite{BEG1994}, with the modern treatment in Curry-Gover \cite{CurryGover2018}; the almost-Einstein characterisation (Einstein metrics as parallel scale tractors) is Gover's \cite{Gover2010}, and Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations} is that characterisation put to a new use: the reading of the GTG vacuum equations as the covariant constancy of an ideal point of the series' completion, and the identification of the parabolic stabiliser structure with the obstruction structure of \cite{ButlerT1}, are the contributions claimed, not tractor calculus itself. The \emph{Kasner} form of the Schwarzschild interior is classical (Kantowski-Sachs), and the velocity-dominated class descends from Eardley-Liang-Sachs \cite{ELS1972} and Isenberg-Moncrief \cite{IsenbergMoncrief1990}; BKL oscillations and the billiard description are \cite{BKL1970, DHN2003}; the weighted limit theorem and its holonomy identification are new. On the Kerr side, the Kerr-Schild form is \cite{KerrSchild1965}, the Killing spinor is Walker-Penrose \cite{WalkerPenrose1970} with Carter's constant \cite{Carter1968}; mass inflation is Poisson-Israel \cite{PoissonIsrael1990}, the $C^0$ stability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon with generic curvature blow-up is Dafermos-Luk \cite{DafermosLuk2017}, and the finiteness of tidal distortion is Ori \cite{Ori1991}. What part three adds is the reading: the location of the framework's own criteria inside these results, and the conclusion they jointly support about the ascent.

title: Setting and conventions
text:
Spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ with orthonormal generators $\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_2, \gamma_3$, $\gamma_0^2 = +1$, $\gamma_i^2 = -1$; in the $(t,r)$ plane write $\et := \gamma_0$, $\er := \gamma_1$. The pseudoscalar is $I := \gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, with $I^2 = -1$; $I$ commutes with every even element and anticommutes with every vector. Units $G = c = 1$; metric signature $(+,-,-,-)$. Curvature conventions are those fixed by the Cartan structure equations exactly as in T5's appendix \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5}; in these conventions the de Sitter metric has $\Ric_{ab} = \Lambda\, g_{ab}$ and scalar curvature $R = 4\Lambda$.

In gauge theory gravity, gravity is a pair of gauge fields on the flat background: the position-dependent linear map $\hb(a)$ on vectors, gauging local frame rescalings, and the connection bivector $\Omega(a)$, gauging local Lorentz rotations. The covariant derivative and field strength are
\[
D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M, \qquad
R(a \wedge b) = a\cdot\nabla\,\Omega(b) - b\cdot\nabla\,\Omega(a) + \Omega(a) \times \Omega(b),
\]
with $A \times B := \tfrac12(AB - BA)$, and the field equations are $R(a) - \tfrac12 a R = \kappa\, T(a)$ together with the vanishing of torsion, which determines $\Omega$ algebraically from $\hb$; the metric is $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ \cite{LDG1998}. Every operation in these displays is interior to $\Cl(1,3)$: nothing invokes a curved manifold beyond the flat background. The theory is a field theory of an invertibility-demanding map, which is exactly the condition the transport principle addresses.

title: The unipotent ray
text: T06 works with the gauge field of the Schwarzschild solution in the Newtonian (Painlev\'e-Gullstrand) gauge exactly as T05 sets it up (\claimref{note.singularity.setting-schwarzschild-gauge-field-connection-where}): the identity minus $\beta$ times the projector $P$, which squares to zero. T06 calls this one-parameter family the unipotent ray and reads it as a trajectory in the gauge group (\claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}).

title: The gauge trajectory is a unipotent ray
proof: Nilpotency: $P^2(a) = P\bigl((a\cdot\et)\er\bigr) = (a\cdot\et)(\er\cdot\et)\,\er = 0$, since $\er \cdot \et = 0$. The group law is bilinearity plus $P^2 = 0$: $(1 + sP)(1 + s'P) = 1 + (s + s')P + ss'P^2$. Inversion is the case $s' = -s$. The metric: $\hb^{-1}(\et) = \et + \beta(\et\cdot\et)\er = \et + \beta\er$, and $\hb^{-1}(\er) = \er$ since $\er \cdot \et = 0$; then $g(\et,\et) = (\et + \beta\er)^2 = \et^2 + \beta^2\er^2 = 1 - \beta^2$ (the cross terms cancel by anticommutation of orthogonal vectors, \claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}), $g(\et,\er) = (\et + \beta\er)\cdot\er = \beta\,\er^2 = -\beta$, and $g(\er,\er) = -1$; the angular generators are untouched by $P$. For (4): the folding computation is short enough to repeat. The null directions of $g$ in the $(t,r)$ plane are the $a = \et + \lambda\er$ with $0 = g(a,a) = 1 - \beta^2 - 2\lambda\beta - \lambda^2 \cdot 1 \cdot (-1)(-1)$; explicitly $g(a,a) = (1-\beta^2) - 2\lambda\beta - \lambda^2$, whose roots are $\lambda = -\beta \pm 1$. As $r \to 0$, $\beta \to \infty$ and both normalised null directions $\tfrac{1}{-\beta\pm1}\et + \er \to \er$: the cone collapses onto the single direction $\er$, the kernel direction, null for the rescaled boundary form in which the collapse is measured \cite[Prop.~2.6]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly}) (for $g$ itself $\er$ has norm $-1$ at every $r > 0$). That the resulting obstruction is type N and forces Rule 1 (\claimref{singularity.type-n-only-type-n}), and that no gauge choice removes it (\claimref{singularity.non-removability-invariant-argument}), is T5's Steps 1-2 \cite{ButlerT5}, quoted here rather than reproved.

title: Parabolic for a structural reason
text: The structural family is the one that recurs throughout the series. Unipotent, null-direction-shearing maps are exactly what obstructed the element-level completion in the no-go theorem of \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1}: the stabiliser of a null direction contains parabolic null rotations, and their fixed-point-free shear excludes every candidate partner. Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray} says the dynamical approach to the singularity proceeds along a parabolic orbit in the gauge group: the gauge field is, at every radius, a finite null-type shear of the identity, and the singularity is the divergence of the shear parameter. The obstruction of the kinematic theory and the trajectory of the dynamical solution belong to the same conjugacy structure. In the section ``Part three, first half: the approach'' this observation is promoted to a theorem: the boundary holonomy of the weighted limit is exactly the Levi factor of the parabolic, with no component in the shearing nilradical.

title: Exact scale decoupling
text: Write $\sigma_r := \er\et$ for the unit radial spacetime bivector, so $\sigma_r^2 = \er\et\er\et = -\er^2\et^2 = +1$, and let $\Pi$ denote the projection of the six-dimensional bivector space onto the plane pair $\operatorname{span}\{\sigma_r, I\sigma_r\}$.

title: Exact scale decoupling
text:
In the conventions of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}, the Schwarzschild curvature operator is, exactly and at every radius,
\[
R(B) \;=\; -\,\frac{M}{r^3}\,S(B), \qquad
S \;:=\; 1 - 3\Pi \;=\; -\tfrac12\bigl(B \mapsto B + 3\,\sigma_r B \sigma_r\bigr),
\]
where the shape operator $S$ satisfies the algebraic identity
\[
S^2 + S = 2 ,
\]
has spectrum $(-2, -2, 1, 1, 1, 1)$, and is trace-free. The factorisation is exact: $S$ depends on neither $M$ nor $r$, and the entire approach to the singularity changes only the conformal prefactor $-M/r^3$.
proof: First the algebra of conjugation by $\sigma_r$. For $B$ in the plane pair: $\sigma_r\,\sigma_r\,\sigma_r = \sigma_r$ since $\sigma_r^2 = 1$; and $\sigma_r (I\sigma_r)\sigma_r = I\,\sigma_r^3 = I\sigma_r$ since $I$ commutes with even elements. For each of the four mixed planes, $B$ anticommutes with $\sigma_r$: writing $B = \gamma_a\gamma_b$ with exactly one index in $\{0,1\}$, the product $\sigma_r B$ reorders by two transpositions against one shared and one distinct generator, producing a net sign $-1$, so $\sigma_r B = -B\sigma_r$ and $\sigma_r B \sigma_r = -B\sigma_r^2 = -B$. Hence $-\tfrac12(B + 3\sigma_r B\sigma_r)$ equals $-2B$ on the plane pair and $+B$ on the mixed planes, which is $1 - 3\Pi$. Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum} says the curvature is diagonal on exactly these planes with eigenvalues $2M/r^3$ (doubled magnitude, on the pair) and $-M/r^3$ (mixed); since $1 - 3\Pi$ has eigenvalues $-2$ on the pair and $+1$ on the mixed planes, the operator with those eigenvalues is exactly $-\tfrac{M}{r^3}(1 - 3\Pi)$: so $R = -(M/r^3)S$ in the conventions of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}, fixed once in the section ``Setting and conventions''; only the eigenvalue ratio $2 : (-1)$ and the identity of the distinguished plane pair enter any later argument, and both are convention-free. The identity: $S^2 = (1 - 3\Pi)^2 = 1 - 6\Pi + 9\Pi^2 = 1 + 3\Pi$ since $\Pi^2 = \Pi$, so $S^2 + S = 2$. Spectrum and trace: eigenvalue $1 - 3 = -2$ on the two-dimensional range of $\Pi$ and $+1$ on its four-dimensional kernel; trace $= 4 - 4 = 0$.

title: Three readings
text: First, the trace-free curvature is pure Weyl, as vacuum requires, and the Weyl part is precisely the conformally covariant part of curvature: what survives the approach is conformal data. Second, dilations emerge exactly, not asymptotically: normalise by the conformal prefactor and nothing along the trajectory changes at all, a rigidity peculiar to the type-D family and stronger than any generic BKL statement. Third, the spectrum exhibits the classic $2{:}1$ Coulombic tidal structure, stretching along the radial plane at twice the rate of the transverse compression; the ratio is an eigenvalue ratio of $S$, hence a conformal invariant of the approach. The singularity is approached with a fixed, scale-free curvature shape, and the divergence is carried entirely by a single conformal weight. The identity $S^2 + S = 2$, equivalently $(S-1)(S+2) = 0$, is the minimal-polynomial statement of this rigidity, and it is the algebraic identity that the complexified Kerr version in the section ``Part three, second half: the Kerr tests'' inherits unchanged, the scale alone becoming complex.

title: Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point
Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point
text: Part one located the failure of division and the conformal rigidity of the approach. This part proves that the ascent $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ is not an operation applied to the field equations from outside: the vacuum equations \emph{are}, exactly and at every radius, a single covariant statement about the rank-six ambient bundle whose fibre algebra is $\Cl(2,4)$. No limit is taken anywhere in this section.

title: The tractor bundle in a scale
text:
Let $M^\circ$ be a region where $\hb$ is invertible, $g$ the physical metric there, and $[g]$ its conformal class. The completion of the series assigns to $[g]$ the ambient (tractor) bundle: the rank-six vector bundle $\mathcal{T}$ which, in the chosen scale $g$, splits as
\[
\mathcal{T} \;\cong\; \R \,\oplus\, TM^\circ \,\oplus\, \R, \qquad \text{sections } (\sigma, \mu^b, \rho),
\]
carrying the tractor metric
\begin{equation}
Q((\sigma,\mu,\rho)) \;=\; g(\mu,\mu) \,+\, 2\sigma\rho .
\end{equation}
With $g$ of signature $(1,3)$ the form $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu) \,+\, 2\sigma\rho$ has signature $(2,4)$: the $\mu$ block contributes $(1,3)$ and the hyperbolic $\sigma\rho$ pairing contributes $(1,1)$. The fibre Clifford algebra is $\Cl(2,4)$ and the structure algebra of the bundle is $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$, acting through the bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$: this is the same completion that Rule 1 forces at the degenerate locus \cite{ButlerT1, ButlerT4}, here assembled over the regular region.

title: Metric parallelism, and the trace of the Schouten condition
text: Let $g$ be the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). (i) The connection \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection}, which on flat spacetime is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, preserves the tractor metric $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu) \,+\, 2\sigma\rho$, the square $Q$ of $\Cl(2,4)$. (ii) If $\Sch_{ab} = c\, g_{ab}$ for a function $c$, that is $\Sch(A) = c\,A$ for the Schouten map of the field strength, then $c = \tfrac{R}{24}$ and $\Ric_{ab} = \tfrac{R}{4} g_{ab}$, that is $\mathcal{R}(A) = \tfrac14\mathcal{R}\,A$; in particular $\Sch_{ab} = 0$ if and only if $\Ric_{ab} = 0$.
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

(i) Along any direction $a$, with primes denoting the slots of \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection},
\[
\tfrac12\,\partial_a Q(T) \;=\; \sigma'\rho + \rho'\sigma + \mu^b\mu'_b
= (\nabla_a\sigma - \mu_a)\rho + (\nabla_a\rho + \Sch_a{}^b\mu_b)\sigma + \mu^b(\nabla_a\mu_b + g_{ab}\rho - \Sch_{ab}\sigma).
\]
The genuine derivative terms assemble to $\tfrac12\partial_a(2\sigma\rho + |\mu|^2)$; the remainder is $-\mu_a\rho + \mu_a \rho + \Sch_a{}^b\mu_b\sigma - \Sch_{ab}\mu^b\sigma = 0$, the two Schouten terms being one contraction written with the index raised on either side, so that no symmetry of $\Sch$ is needed.
(ii) Tracing $\Sch_{ab} = c\,g_{ab}$ gives $4c = \tfrac12(R - \tfrac{4R}{6}) = \tfrac{R}{6}$, so $c = \tfrac{R}{24}$; substituting back, $\Ric_{ab} = \tfrac{R}{6}g_{ab} + 2c\,g_{ab} = \tfrac{R}{4}g_{ab}$. If $c = 0$ then $R = 24c = 0$ and hence $\Ric = 0$; the converse is immediate.

title: Part three, first half: the approach
Part three, first half: the approach
text: Part two established that the vacuum equations are a parallel ideal point, exactly and at every radius where $\hb$ is invertible. The remaining question is whether the covariant description survives where the metric one fails: does the tractor formulation extend to the singular locus itself? This section proves that it does, for the class of singularities containing Schwarzschild, under a blow-up whose direction-dependent weights the geometry itself selects, and it identifies exactly what algebra survives at the boundary. Throughout the section we work in the interior $0 < r < 2M$ and, where convenient, in units $2M = 1$; every expansion below is an identity of exact power series in $\sqrt{r}$ with rational coefficients, and the verification script checks the stated coefficients in exact arithmetic.

title: Kasner form of the interior
text:
In the interior, with $A(r) := 2M/r - 1 > 0$, the Schwarzschild gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), taken in a synchronous position gauge, has derived metric of diagonal form
\[
ds^2 \;=\; d\tau^2 - A\,dt^2 - r^2\,d\Omega^2,
\qquad
\tau(r) \;=\; \int_0^r A(u)^{-1/2}\,du ,
\]
where $\tau$ is proper time along the radial timelike worldlines ruling the interior, whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel (the geodesics of the derived metric), normalised so that the singularity is $\tau = 0$. In units $2M = 1$,
\[
\tau(r) \;=\; \tfrac23\, r^{3/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}\,r + O(r^2)\bigr),
\qquad
r \;=\; R\,\bigl(1 - \tfrac15 R + O(R^2)\bigr), \quad R := (3\tau/2)^{2/3},
\]
and the scale factors obey $\sqrt{A} \propto \tau^{-1/3}$ and $r \propto \tau^{2/3}$ to leading order: the Kasner exponents of the approach are
\[
(p_1, p_2, p_3) \;=\; \bigl(-\tfrac13,\ \tfrac23,\ \tfrac23\bigr),
\qquad
p_1 + p_2 + p_3 \;=\; 1, \qquad p_1^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 \;=\; 1 .
\]
proof:
The proof works with the derived metric $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ and its geodesics, read in Gauge Theory Gravity by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i) and (iii). Inside the horizon $f = 1 - 2M/r$ is negative, so $r$ is the timelike coordinate: writing the static form of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum} in the interior and substituting $d\tau = A^{-1/2}dr$ gives the displayed synchronous form, with $t$ now a spatial coordinate and $A = -f$. The curves of constant $(t,\theta,\varphi)$ are unit-speed timelike geodesics (synchronous form: $g_{\tau\tau} = 1$ and $g$ is $\tau$-orthogonal, so $\Gamma^\mu{}_{\tau\tau} = 0$). The expansion: in units $2M = 1$, $A = (1-r)/r$ and
\[
\tau(r) = \int_0^r \sqrt{\frac{u}{1-u}}\,du
= \int_0^r u^{1/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac12 u + \tfrac38 u^2 + \cdots\bigr)\,du
= \tfrac23 r^{3/2} + \tfrac15 r^{5/2} + O(r^{7/2}),
\]
which is the first display; the binomial series converges on $0 \le u \le r < 1$. Inversion: $(3\tau/2)^{2/3} = r(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}r + O(r^2))^{2/3} = r(1 + \tfrac15 r + O(r^2))$, so $R = r + \tfrac15 r^2 + O(r^3)$, and reverting this series gives $r = R(1 - \tfrac15 R + O(R^2))$. Leading behaviour: $\sqrt A = r^{-1/2}\sqrt{1-r} \propto \tau^{-1/3}$ and $r \propto \tau^{2/3}$ by the displayed inversion. The exponent identities $\sum p_i = \sum p_i^2 = 1$ are the arithmetic $-\tfrac13 + \tfrac23 + \tfrac23 = 1$ and $\tfrac19 + \tfrac49 + \tfrac49 = 1$: the approach is an exact member of the Kasner family to leading order, the axial exponent negative, the sphere directions shared.

title: Exact parallelism, and the convergence rate
proof:
The proof computes with the Christoffel symbols of the derived metric; by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) these are $g^\rho \cdot D_{e_\mu} g_\nu$, so vanishing of the covariant derivative below is $D$-parallelism of the physical frame. (1) For a synchronous diagonal metric $d\tau^2 - \sum_i a_i^2 (dx^i)^2$ the only Christoffel symbols with a $\tau$ index are $\Gamma^i{}_{\tau i} = \partial_\tau \log a_i$ and $\Gamma^\tau{}_{ii} = a_i\,\partial_\tau a_i$ (no sum), so
\[
\nabla_{\partial_\tau}\bigl(a_i^{-1}\partial_i\bigr)
= (\partial_\tau a_i^{-1})\,\partial_i + a_i^{-1}\,\Gamma^j{}_{\tau i}\,\partial_j
= -a_i^{-2}(\partial_\tau a_i)\,\partial_i + a_i^{-2}(\partial_\tau a_i)\,\partial_i = 0 ,
\]
identically in $\tau$; and $\nabla_{\partial_\tau}\partial_\tau = 0$ as noted in Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}. Here $a_1 = \sqrt{A(\tau)}$, $a_2 = r(\tau)$, $a_3 = r(\tau)\sin\theta$; the $\theta$-dependence of $a_3$ does not enter $\partial_\tau$-derivatives, so the computation applies at each fixed angular position. (2) From $\partial_\tau = \sqrt{A}\,\partial_r$: $\sigma_1 = \sqrt A\,\partial_r \log\sqrt A = A'/(2\sqrt A)$, and with $A = (1-r)/r$, $A' = -1/r^2$, this is $\sigma_1 = -\tfrac12 r^{-3/2}(1-r)^{-1/2}$; likewise $\sigma_2 = \sqrt A / r = r^{-3/2}\sqrt{1-r}$. Multiplying by the series for $\tau$ from Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}:
\[
\tau\sigma_1 = -\tfrac13\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}r\bigr)\bigl(1 + \tfrac12 r\bigr) + O(r^2) = -\tfrac13 - \tfrac{4}{15}r + O(r^2),
\]
\[
\tau\sigma_2 = \tfrac23\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}r\bigr)\bigl(1 - \tfrac12 r\bigr) + O(r^2) = \tfrac23 - \tfrac{2}{15}r + O(r^2),
\]
and substituting $r = R(1 + O(R))$ leaves the displayed constants unchanged at this order. All manipulations are compositions and reversions of power series in $\sqrt r$ with rational coefficients; the script performs them exactly and confirms every printed coefficient. (3) The scale factors: $a_1 = r^{-1/2}\sqrt{1-r}$ and its Kasner comparison $c_1\tau^{-1/3}$ differ by the relative factor $\sqrt{1-r}\,(1 + O(r)) = 1 + O(r) = 1 + O(\tau^{2/3})$, and likewise $a_2 = r$ against $c_2\tau^{2/3}$; the rates are the $\sigma_i$ of part (2), whose relative deviations from $p_i/\tau$ are the displayed $O(\tau^{2/3})$; and the intrinsic curvature of the $S^2$ sections is $r^{-2} = O(\tau^{-4/3})$, a relative $O(\tau^{2/3})$ against the dominant curvature scale $\tau^{-2}$. One rate governs all three items. One-signedness: near $r = 0$ each deviation is a convergent power series in $\sqrt r$ (every manipulation above is a composition or reversion of such series, convergent on $0 \le r < 1$), so it either vanishes identically or carries a nonzero leading coefficient whose sign it takes on a punctured neighbourhood of $0$: each deviation is one-signed for small $\tau$, and no oscillation occurs anywhere in the class.

title: The interior connection, exactly
text:
In the parallel frame of Lemma \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}, write $B_i := e_0 \wedge e_i$ for the three boost bivectors and $R_{ij} := e_i \wedge e_j$ for the rotations. The rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ of the interior gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}: the torsion-free connection, whose reading on the derived metric is its Levi-Civita connection), evaluated on the unit tangential physical directions (through $A \cdot D = D_{\hb(A)}$, so that $\Omega(e_c)$ stands for $\Omega(\hb(e_c))$), is exactly
\[
\Omega(e_1) = -\sigma_1 B_1, \qquad
\Omega(e_2) = -\sigma_2 B_2, \qquad
\Omega(e_3) = -\sigma_3 B_3 + \frac{\cot\theta}{r}\,R_{23},
\]
and $\Omega(e_0) = 0$, in the sign of the Definition, $D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M$, in which the Cartan forms $\omega^{i}{}_{0} = \sigma_i\,\theta^i$ assemble to $-\sigma_i B_i$. The rotation coefficient is the connection induced by $D$ on the round two-spheres of fixed $(\tau, t)$, of radius $r$: in any local orthonormal frame on an $S^2$ coordinate patch its coefficients are $O(1/r)$.
proof: The computation below is written for the derived metric of the interior gravitational field; by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) its Levi-Civita connection forms, evaluated on the frame and assembled into bivectors, are the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ on the physical frame vectors, so it computes $\Omega$ directly. With orthonormal coframe $\theta^0 = d\tau$, $\theta^i = a_i dx^i$, dual to the frame of \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}, the first structure equation $d\theta^a = -\omega^a{}_b \wedge \theta^b$ determines the connection uniquely (torsion-free, metric). Computing: $d\theta^1 = (\partial_\tau a_1)\,d\tau \wedge dt = \sigma_1\,\theta^0 \wedge \theta^1$, and likewise for $\theta^2$; while $d\theta^3 = \partial_\tau(a_3)\,d\tau\wedge d\varphi\,+\,\partial_\theta(r\sin\theta)\,d\theta \wedge d\varphi = \sigma_3\,\theta^0\wedge\theta^3 + \frac{\cot\theta}{r}\,\theta^2 \wedge \theta^3$. Matching term by term gives $\omega^i{}_0 = \sigma_i\,\theta^i$ (no sum) and $\omega^3{}_2 = \frac{\cot\theta}{r}\,\theta^3$, with all other independent components zero; uniqueness of the Levi-Civita connection closes the argument. Evaluating on the unit vectors and assembling into bivectors in the sign of the Definition ($D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M$: the form $\omega^i{}_0 = \sigma_i\,\theta^i$ gives the boost term $-\sigma_i B_i$, and $\omega^3{}_2$ gives $+\frac{\cot\theta}{r}R_{23}$) gives the display. The last sentence is the standard statement that the induced connection on the constant-$\tau$ spheres is that of $S^2$ of radius $r$, whose coefficients in an orthonormal frame scale as $1/r$; the $\cot\theta$ divergence at the poles is an artifact of the spherical frame, removable by a change of patch.

title: The boosts generate exactly the Levi factor
text:
Inside $\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathfrak{so}(2,4)$, in the notation of Proposition \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model} with $W = \operatorname{span}(e_0, e_1, e_2, e_3)$, the Lie algebra generated by the three boosts $\{B_1, B_2, B_3\}$ is exactly $\Lambda^2 W \cong \mathfrak{so}(1,3)$: six-dimensional, containing all three rotations, and containing no component in $
Inf \wedge W$, $
O \wedge W$, or $\R(
Inf\wedge
O)$.
proof:
Containment is immediate: $B_i \in \Lambda^2 W$ and $\Lambda^2 W$ is a subalgebra (brackets of operators preserving $W$ and annihilating $W^\perp$ do the same). For fullness, compute with $(u \wedge v)(w) \;=\; \ip{v}{w}\,u - \ip{u}{w}\,v$, the action of bivectors on vectors as the orthogonal Lie algebra (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}): for $u,v,u',v'$ orthogonal frame vectors,
\[
[\,u\wedge v,\ v\wedge w\,] \;=\; Q(v)\; u\wedge w ,
\]
and brackets of wedges with no shared factor vanish. Hence $[B_1, B_2] = [e_0\wedge e_1,\, e_0 \wedge e_2]$: rewriting $B_1 = -e_1\wedge e_0$, this is $-Q(e_0)\, e_1\wedge e_2 = -R_{12}$, and cyclically for the other pairs: all three rotations appear. Then $[R_{12}, B_2] = [e_1\wedge e_2, e_0\wedge e_2]$ $= -[e_1\wedge e_2,\, e_2\wedge e_0] = -Q(e_2)\,e_1\wedge e_0 = -B_1$ recovers the boosts, and the six elements $\{B_i, R_{ij}\}$ are a basis of $\Lambda^2 W$. The verification script performs the generation exactly: starting from the three boosts as antisymmetric matrices over $\mathbb{Q}$ preserving the $(2,4)$ form, it closes under commutators and confirms the resulting span has dimension six and lies in $\Lambda^2 W$.

title: Weighted blow-up, Hubble normalisation, and the admissible class
text:
Blow up the interior along the singular locus by adjoining the exceptional boundary $\{\tau = 0\}$ to the collar $(0,\tau_0] \times \mathcal{B}$, $\mathcal{B} := \R_t \times S^2$, \emph{with direction-dependent weights} $(p_1, p_2, p_3)$: the boundary is probed by the rescaled (Hubble-normalised) data
\[
\widehat\Omega_\tau \;:=\; \tau\,\Omega\big|_{\text{unit tangential directions at time } \tau},
\]
the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ in the $D$-parallel physical frame, evaluated on the unit vectors of the $\tau$-slice and multiplied by $\tau$; a tangential direction carries weight $p_i$ in the sense that its unit vector contracts by the factor $\tau^{p_i}$ relative to the coordinate vector, which is exactly what the frame normalisation implements. A gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on the collar (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), in a synchronous gauge and with derived metric singular at $\tau = 0$, is \emph{admissible} (Einstein velocity-dominated) if it is Einstein, $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ with $\Lambda$ constant (in the store's sign, so that the derived metric has $\Ric_{ab} = \Lambda\, g_{ab}$; the field-equation hypothesis the tractor clauses of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} consume; the Levi-Civita clauses, those about $\Omega$, use only the decay conditions), and in some $D$-parallel orthonormal physical frame, with boosts $B_i = e_0 \wedge e_i$, the Hubble-normalised connection satisfies $\widehat\Omega_\tau = -\sum_i p_i B_i \otimes \hat\theta^i + E_\tau$ with constants $p_i \neq 0$ (the sign is that of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, $D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M$, in which the Cartan forms $\omega^{i}{}_{0} = (p_i/\tau)\,\theta^i$ of a Kasner field assemble to $-\sum_i p_i B_i$) satisfying the Kasner-type constraint $\sum_i p_i^2 = 1$ (the Schwarzschild exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ satisfy it, Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}; the constraint is what Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} uses, through Cauchy-Schwarz, to bound the model generator on unit directions by $1$) and an error $E_\tau$ which tends to zero as $\tau \to 0$ and for which $\|E_\tau\|/\tau$ is integrable on $(0, \tau_0]$, both locally uniformly on $\mathcal{B}$. A synchronous metric is called admissible when it is the derived metric of an admissible gravitational field. Two boundary objects are part of the same data. The \emph{boundary bundle} is the trivial extension of the parallel trivialisation: the tractor fibre in the parallel tractor frame, extended over $\{\tau = 0\} \times \mathcal{B}$ as a product, so that a section defined for $\tau > 0$ extends to the boundary exactly when its components in that frame converge. The \emph{boundary holonomy algebra} is the Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ generated by the limiting values of the Hubble-normalised connection on unit tangential directions, over all boundary points: a values-level definition, which is what the theorem computes; along the directions where the connection is abelian it agrees with the transport-level reading (Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}, final clause). By Lemmas \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate} and \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly} the Schwarzschild interior ($\Lambda = 0$) is admissible, with $\|E_\tau\| = O(\tau^{2/3}) + O(\tau/r) = O(\tau^{1/3})$ tending to zero and $\|E_\tau\|/\tau = O(\tau^{-2/3})$ integrable at $0$. On the sphere factor the frame, and with it the display, is taken patchwise (no global orthonormal frame on $S^2$ exists); admissibility and the limiting values are patch-independent statements, the values transforming by the constant rotation between patches.

title: Weighted limit theorem
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

Rotation part: by Lemma \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly} the rotation coefficients on unit directions are $O(1/r)$, so Hubble-normalised they are $O(	au/r) = O(	au^{1/3}) 	o 0$. Tractor connection: the Einstein hypothesis of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} gives $\Sch_{ab} = 	frac{\Lambda}{6}\,g_{ab}$ in the scale $g$ (Lemma \claimref{interior.metric-parallelism-trace-schouten-condition}(ii), Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}), so by \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection} the tractor connection is the Levi-Civita action on the $\mu$-slot plus coupling maps ($\mu \mapsto -\mu_a$ into the $\sigma$-slot, $ho \mapsto g_{ab}ho$ and $\sigma \mapsto -	frac{\Lambda}{6}g_{ab}\sigma$ into the $\mu$-slot, $\mu \mapsto 	frac{\Lambda}{6}\mu_a$ into the $ho$-slot) whose coefficients on unit directions are $	au$-independent, so their Hubble normalisation is $O(	au) 	o 0$; without a field-equation hypothesis the Schouten term is not controlled relative to $g$ and no such statement holds, which is why the hypothesis is part of admissibility. The computed algebra is the same for every $\Lambda$; only its identification as a Levi factor is a $\Lambda = 0$ statement. Final clause: by Lemma \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly} the connection along the $t$-lines is $-\sigma_1 B_1\,	heta^1$ and along the $	heta$-lines is $-\sigma_2 B_2\,	heta^2$, in each case a fixed bivector times a scalar form, so all transports in one such direction commute. Hubble-normalised, the interior generator on the unit direction is $-(	au\sigma_i)B_i$ against the model's $-p_iB_i$, and $	au\sigma_i - p_i = O(	au^{2/3})$ by Lemma \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}(2): over segments of fixed Hubble-normalised length the transports differ by a boost of angle $O(	au^{2/3}) 	o 0$. Over a fixed \emph{coordinate} segment the generator is $-(\partial_	au a_i)B_i$, of size $	au^{p_i - 1}$, the transports individually diverge, and no claim is made about their comparison. The frame comparison along the $	au$-geodesics is a separate scalar computation: $\int_0^	au(\sigma_i - p_i/s)\,ds = \log igl(a_i(	au)\,	au^{-p_i}/c_i igr)$ with $c_i := \lim_{s 	o 0} a_i(s)\,s^{-p_i}$, finite and nonzero by Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}, so the coordinate frame's evolution converges to the model's at rate $O(	au^{2/3})$, direction by direction, with no noncommutativity anywhere in the argument. Along the $\varphi$-lines the connection on the coordinate vector $\partial_\varphi$ is $(\partial_	au a_3)\,B_3 + \cos	heta\,R_{23}$ (Lemma \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly}), a divergent boost beside a $	au$-independent rotation, and the two do not commute: a Duhamel comparison would conjugate the $O(	au^{1/3})$ discrepancy by an unbounded model transport, which the integrability hypothesis alone does not control, so no transport-level claim is made in that direction here; Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} and Corollary \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-lines-exactly} below make it, for segments of fixed Hubble-normalised length, where the conjugation is harmless.
