title: The parabolic structure, completed
text: The theorem completes the argument announced in Remark \claimref{note.interior.parabolic-structural-reason}. The stabiliser of the covariantly constant ideal point is the parabolic with Levi factor $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ and nilradical $\R^4$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model}); the weighted limit gives nonzero limiting values in the boost part of the Levi factor, which generates it, and zero in the nilradical, which consists of the very shear directions whose transvection action obstructed the element-level completion in \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1}. Three appearances of one structure are now related: the parabolic obstruction of the no-go theorem, the unipotent gauge trajectory of Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}, and the Levi boundary holonomy of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}. At the singularity the limiting connection lies purely in the Levi factor of the stabiliser of a frozen ideal point.

title: The generic delimiter: mixmaster
text: The theorem's scope is the admissible (Einstein velocity-dominated) class, which contains the Schwarzschild and Schwarzschild-de Sitter interiors and the vacuum Kasner models with $p_i \neq 0$, and the scope boundary is a result, not a caveat. For generic oscillatory (BKL, mixmaster) singularities the Hubble-normalised frame undergoes infinitely many Kasner-axis rotations, so parallel transport of the frame has no limit at all, and no theorem of the present form can hold framewise: the admissibility integral of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} diverges. \emph{Provenance for the generic case:} the oscillatory approach is \cite{BKL1970}, its billiard formulation \cite{DHN2003}; velocity-dominated asymptotics in the sense used here descend from \cite{ELS1972, IsenbergMoncrief1990}. The correct generic statement must be formulated on the quotient by the Kasner-axis dynamics, the cosmological billiard, and formulating a billiard-invariant weighted limit theorem is posed in the section ``Scope, and successor problems'' as a successor problem. The delimiter locates exactly where the present method ends and names the invariant object that should replace the frame.

title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter weighted limit
text: For the Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), in the synchronous gauge with $A(r) = 2M/r + \Lambda r^2/3 - 1 > 0$ near $r = 0$, every function of its derived metric expressed in Kasner time acquires relative corrections of order $\Lambda r^3/M \propto \Lambda\tau^2$ against the Schwarzschild case. Consequently the Hubble-normalised connection differs from the Schwarzschild one by $O(\Lambda\tau^2)$, strictly subdominant to the $O(\tau^{2/3})$ recovery rate, and Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} holds verbatim: identical Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$, identical boundary data, identical convergence rate. The holonomy clause is upgraded rather than weakened: for $\Lambda > 0$ the limit algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ now lies inside the \emph{reductive} stabiliser $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ of the non-null parallel tractor (parallel for the $\Cl(2,4)$ tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}) of Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, and the vanishing of the nilradical component is automatic: there is no nilradical.
proof: The function $A$ below is that of the derived metric of the gravitational field, and the rates $\sigma_i$ are read from $\Omega$ in the physical frame, by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i) and (ii). In units $2M = 1$, $A = \tfrac{1}{r}\bigl(1 - r + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}r^3\bigr)$: the $\Lambda$ term enters every occurrence of $A$ through the factor $1 - r + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}r^3$, a relative correction of order $\Lambda r^3$ against the Schwarzschild factor $1 - r$, uniformly on $r \le r_0 < 1$. The proper-time integral, its inversion, and the rates $\tau\sigma_i$ are the same power-series manipulations as in Lemmas \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior} and \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate} with $(1-u)$ replaced by $(1 - u + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}u^3)$; since the new term has degree three, every printed coefficient through order $R$ is unchanged and the first $\Lambda$-dependent correction enters at relative order $r^3 \propto \tau^2$. The script verifies this exactly: expanding both series with $\Lambda$ as a formal rational parameter, the coefficients through order $r^{2}$ agree identically and the first disagreement carries the factor $\Lambda/3$ at order $r^3$. The connection statement follows as in Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}(1), with the additional remark that the tractor couplings now carry the Schouten term $\Sch_{ab} = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}g_{ab}$ (Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}), a $\tau$-independent coefficient on unit directions, Hubble-normalised to $O(\tau) \to 0$ exactly as before; and the parallel section is now $I_g = (1, 0, \tfrac{\Lambda}{6})$, parallel at every $\tau > 0$, extending by the same constant-section argument: its $\mu$-component vanishes, so every limiting value annihilates it. The holonomy clause: the limiting values are the same weighted boosts, generating $\Lambda^2 W \cong \mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ by Lemma \claimref{interior.boosts-generate-exactly-levi-factor}; for $\Lambda > 0$ the stabiliser of $I_g$ is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ by Proposition \claimref{interior.non-null-stabilisers-section-they-act}, reductive, and $\Lambda^2 W \subset \Lambda^2(I_g^\perp)$ since $W \perp I_g$; the nilradical statement is Proposition \claimref{interior.non-null-stabilisers-section-they-act}(1).

title: What the two ends of the geometry jointly say
text: The frozen point governs both ends of the geometry, in opposite algebraic ways. At infinity, its stabiliser is rotated from parabolic to reductive by $\Lambda$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}): the obstruction structure at infinity is removed by the cosmological constant. At the singularity, the approach gives nonzero limiting values in the boost part of the Levi factor, which generates it, and zero in the nilradical, for $\Lambda = 0$ and $\Lambda \neq 0$ alike (Theorems \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}, \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}): the obstruction structure at the singularity is intact, and the weighted limit resolves it by transporting the description, not by removing the obstruction. This division is the geometric instance of the series' one-way door: what is obstructed is never repaired in place, and what survives is the conformal, ascended data.

title: Transport along tangential curves, and the $\varphi$-lines
text:
Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} proves transport-level convergence along the $t$- and $\theta$-coordinate lines and makes no claim along the $\varphi$-lines, where a divergent boost appears alongside a fixed rotation. This subsection shows that the missing claim concerns coordinate segments, not transport: along every tangential curve of fixed Hubble-normalised length the transport converges to the model's, for every admissible metric, by an elementary bound that needs nothing beyond admissibility; and at Schwarzschild the $\varphi$-lines converge with the explicit rate $\tau^{1/3}$.

Fix on $\mathrm{End}(\R^{6}) \supset \mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ the operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm on $\R^{6}$ in which the adapted tractor frame is orthonormal; it is submultiplicative with $\|1\| = 1$, and each $B_i$ and each rotation $R_{ij}$, whose matrix in that frame has a single pair of entries $\pm 1$ in an off-diagonal $2 \times 2$ block, has $\|B_i\| = \|R_{ij}\| = 1$. A \emph{tangential curve at time $\tau$} is a smooth curve $\gamma$ in the slice $\{\tau\} \times \mathcal{B}$, parametrised by its own Hubble-normalised arclength $s$ (physical arclength divided by $\tau$), with unit tangent $u(s) = \sum_{i} u^{i}(s) e_{i}$, $\sum (u^{i})^{2} = 1$. Its \emph{transport} $T_{\gamma}(\lambda)$ is the solution of $T' = G(s) T$, $T(0) = 1$, on $[0, \lambda]$, with $G(s) = \widehat\Omega_{\tau}(u(s))$ the Hubble-normalised connection of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} on the unit tangent; its \emph{model transport} $T^{0}_{\gamma}(\lambda)$ solves the same equation with $H(s) = -\sum_{i} u^{i}(s)\, p_{i} B_{i}$, the limiting connection $\widehat\Omega_0$ evaluated on the same unit tangent.

title: Transport-level convergence along tangential curves, all admissible gravitational fields
text:
Let the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on the collar be admissible (Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}), $K \subset \mathcal{B}$ compact, and $\gamma$ a tangential curve at time $\tau$ inside $K$ of Hubble-normalised length $\lambda$, with $T_\gamma$ its $D$-transport and $T^0_\gamma$ that of the Kasner model. Then
\[
\|T_{\gamma}(\lambda) - T^{0}_{\gamma}(\lambda)\| \;\le\; \lambda\, \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}\; \exp\bigl(\lambda\,(1 + \|E_{\tau}\|_{K})\bigr),
\qquad \|E_{\tau}\|_{K} := \sup_{K}\|E_{\tau}\| ,
\]
which tends to zero as $\tau \to 0$, uniformly over all such curves of length at most $\lambda$. No control of the model transport's conjugation of the error is used.
proof:
Along $\gamma$, $G(s) - H(s) = E_{\tau}(u(s))$ by the admissibility display of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}, so $\|G - H\| \le \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}$ pointwise; and $\|H(s)\| \le \sum_{i} |u^{i}| |p_{i}| \|B_{i}\| \le \bigl(\sum_i (u^{i})^{2}\bigr)^{1/2} \bigl(\sum_i p_{i}^{2}\bigr)^{1/2} = 1$ by Cauchy-Schwarz, using $\|B_i\| = 1$ and the constraint $\sum_i p_{i}^{2} = 1$ of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}; so $\|G\| \le 1 + \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}$ and $\|H\| \le 1$. For two linear equations $T' = GT$, $T_{0}' = HT_{0}$ with $T(0) = T_{0}(0) = 1$, the variation-of-constants identity is
\[
T(\lambda) - T_{0}(\lambda) \;=\; \int_{0}^{\lambda} T(\lambda)\,T(s)^{-1}\,\bigl(G(s) - H(s)\bigr)\,T_{0}(s)\,ds ,
\]
which is verified by differentiating in $\lambda$: since $\partial_{\lambda}\bigl(T(\lambda)T(s)^{-1}\bigr) = G(\lambda)T(\lambda)T(s)^{-1}$, the integral $X(\lambda)$ has derivative $G(\lambda)X(\lambda) + (G(\lambda) - H(\lambda))T_{0}(\lambda)$, and $T - T_{0}$ satisfies the same equation $X' = GX + (G - H)T_{0}$ with the same initial value $0$; uniqueness for linear equations closes the identity. Gronwall's inequality in its integral form gives $\|T(\lambda)T(s)^{-1}\| \le \exp(\int_{s}^{\lambda}\|G\|)$ and also $\|T_{0}(s)\| \le \exp(\int_{0}^{s}\|H\|)$, since each is the solution of a linear equation with generator bounded by the stated integrand and initial value $1$. The product $\|T(\lambda)T(s)^{-1}\|\,\|T_{0}(s)\|$ is therefore at most $\exp(\int_{s}^{\lambda}\|G\| + \int_{0}^{s}\|H\|) \le \exp(\lambda(1 + \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}))$, the two integrals covering $[0, \lambda]$ once between them with both integrands bounded by $1 + \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}$; multiplying by $\|G(s) - H(s)\| \le \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}$ and integrating over $[0, \lambda]$ gives the display. Uniformity in the curve is uniformity of the bound in $\gamma$; the limit is the hypothesis $E_{\tau} \to 0$ locally uniformly.

title: Transport along tangential curves, and the $\varphi$-lines
text: The theorem is elementary, and its point is exactly that: the transport-level statement along tangential curves of fixed Hubble-normalised length needs nothing beyond what admissibility already supplies. Control of the model transport's conjugation of the comparison error, weight by weight, would be needed for a comparison over segments of fixed \emph{coordinate} length, whose Hubble-normalised length diverges as $\tau^{p_{i} - 1}$ and along which both transports individually diverge; that comparison is disclaimed in the proof of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} and no claim is made about it here either.

title: The Schwarzschild $\varphi$-lines, exactly
text:
For the Schwarzschild interior in units $2M = 1$, along a $\varphi$-coordinate line at fixed $(r, \theta)$ the Hubble-normalised generator is constant along the line,
\begin{align*}
G \;&=\; -\bigl(\tfrac23 + \delta(r)\bigr) B_{3} + \varepsilon(r)\, R_{23}, \\
\delta(r) \;&=\; \tau\sigma_{3} - \tfrac23 \;=\; -\tfrac{2}{15}\,r - \tfrac{8}{105}\,r^{2} - \tfrac{16}{315}\,r^{3} - \cdots, \\
\varepsilon(r) \;&=\; \frac{\tau\cot\theta}{r} \;=\; \tfrac23\cot\theta\; r^{1/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10} r + \tfrac{9}{56} r^{2} + \cdots\bigr),
\end{align*}
so the transport over a segment of Hubble-normalised length $\lambda$ is the single exponential $\exp(\lambda G)$, the model transport is $\exp(-\tfrac23\lambda B_{3})$, and
\[
\|\exp(\lambda G) - \exp(-\tfrac23\lambda B_{3})\| \;\le\; \lambda\,(|\delta(r)| + |\varepsilon(r)|)\,e^{\lambda(1 + |\delta| + |\varepsilon|)} \;=\; O(r^{1/2}) \;=\; O(\tau^{1/3}) .
\]
The rate is $\tau^{1/3}$, slower than the $\theta$-line's $\tau^{2/3}$, and it is the sphere's intrinsic connection that sets it. Along all tangential curves of fixed Hubble-normalised length the bound of Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} applies with $\|E_{\tau}\|_{K} = O(\tau^{1/3})$ away from the poles. The tangential regularity of the boundary data on the exceptional set holds by symmetry: the data are $SO(3) \times \R_{t}$-invariant, hence constant along $\mathcal{B}$ in an invariant frame and smooth in any patch.
proof: Constancy: the coefficients $\sigma_{3}(r)$ and $\cot\theta/r$ of Lemma \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly}'s $\Omega(e_{3})$ do not depend on $\varphi$, and the unit tangent along the line is $e_{3}$ throughout, so $G(s)$ is constant and the linear equation is solved by the exponential. The series: $\tau\sigma_{3} = \tau\,\partial_{\tau}\log r = \tau\sqrt{A}/r$ with $A = 1/r - 1$; writing $\tau = \tfrac23 r^{3/2} S(r)$ with $S(r) = \tfrac32 r^{-3/2}\int_{0}^{r} u^{1/2}(1-u)^{-1/2}\,du = \sum_{k} \tfrac{3}{2}\binom{-1/2}{k}(-1)^{k}\frac{r^{k}}{k + 3/2}$, one has $\tau\sigma_{3} = \tfrac23 S(r)\sqrt{1 - r}$ and $\varepsilon = \tfrac23 \cot\theta\, r^{1/2} S(r)$; the script computes $S = 1 + \tfrac{3}{10} r + \tfrac{9}{56} r^{2} + \tfrac{5}{48} r^{3} + \cdots$ and the product exactly to order eight, reproducing Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}'s $\tfrac{3}{10}$ and Lemma \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}'s leading $-\tfrac{2}{15}$ (there written in $R = (3\tau/2)^{2/3} = r + O(r^{2})$), with every printed coefficient of $\delta$ negative. The exponential bound is the identity $e^{X} - e^{Y} = \int_{0}^{1} e^{(1-t)X}(X - Y)e^{tY}\,dt$ (the case of constant generators of the proof of Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves}) with $\|X\|, \|Y\| \le \lambda(\tfrac23 + |\delta| + |\varepsilon|) \le \lambda(1 + |\delta| + |\varepsilon|)$, since $\|B_3\| = \|R_{23}\| = 1$. Rates: $r = (3\tau/2)^{2/3}(1 + O(\tau^{2/3}))$ by Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}, so $r = O(\tau^{2/3})$ and $r^{1/2} = O(\tau^{1/3})$. The symmetry statement: the Schwarzschild interior is invariant under $SO(3)$ acting on $S^{2}$ and under $t$-translation, the parallel frame of Lemma \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate} is carried to itself up to the constant patch rotation, and the boundary data, being limits of invariant quantities in that frame, are invariant functions on $\mathcal{B}$, hence constant. The script also carries one floating-point CONTROL check, marked as such and printing its intermediate ratios, which enters no exact check: the operator-norm distance halves when $r$ is quartered at three latitudes, and a fixed coordinate segment $\Delta\varphi = 0.1$ diverges, confirming the disclaimer rather than contradicting it.

title: What is closed, and what remains
text: Of the two halves of the edge-regularity problem, the transport-level half is closed by Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} for every admissible metric, in the only reading in which a transport-level statement can hold (fixed Hubble-normalised length), and the $\varphi$-line clause is closed at Schwarzschild with its rate by Corollary \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-lines-exactly}. The tangential-regularity half is closed at Schwarzschild by symmetry and remains open in general: it asks for tangential derivatives of $E_{\tau}$, which admissibility does not control. The billiard-invariant limit of Remark \claimref{note.interior.generic-delimiter-mixmaster} is the generic-singularity extension and does not bear on any statement made at Schwarzschild.

title: Part three, second half: the Kerr tests
Part three, second half: the Kerr tests
text: Schwarzschild is the case the framework was built for: spherical, static, type D with a point-centred singularity. Kerr is the test. Rotation replaces the point by a ring, adds an inner (Cauchy) horizon whose instability is a classical theme of mathematical relativity, and destroys none, some, or all of the structure of Parts one and two according to how robust that structure is. This section runs the test at three levels: exactly (the algebra of the Kerr gauge field), structurally (where the framework's own criterion locates the singularity), and dynamically (what survives generic perturbation at the Cauchy horizon). The conclusions are collected in the section ``Scope, and successor problems''.

title: Imported: the Kerr-Schild form of the Kerr gauge field
text:
The Kerr solution admits a gauge in which the gauge field is
\[
\hb(a) \;=\; a + H(x)\,(a\cdot k)\,k ,
\]
with $k$ a null vector field tangent to the ingoing principal null congruence, $k^2 = 0$, and $H$ a scalar function ($H = Mr^3/(r^4 + a^2\cos^2\theta\, r^2)$ in Boyer-Lindquist-adapted oblate coordinates; only $k^2 = 0$ enters the algebra below). Schwarzschild is the case $a = 0$ in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein form. \emph{Provenance:} Kerr-Schild \cite{KerrSchild1965}; the GTG form \cite[Ch.~14]{DoranLasenby2003}, \cite{LDG1998}.
provenance: R. P. Kerr and A. Schild, Some algebraically degenerate solutions of Einstein's gravitational field equations, Proc. Symp. Appl. Math. 17 (1965), 199--209.; C. Doran and A. Lasenby, Geometric Algebra for Physicists, Cambridge University Press (2003)., Ch.~14; A. Lasenby, C. Doran and S. Gull, Gravity, gauge theories and geometric algebra, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A 356 (1998), 487--582.

title: Unipotency across the Kerr family
proof: (1) $P_k^2(a) = P_k\bigl((a\cdot k)k\bigr) = (a\cdot k)\,(Q(k))\,k = 0$ since $k^2 = 0$; the group law and the closed-form inverse follow exactly as in Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}, with parameter $s = H$ varying over the manifold. (2) Expand: $\hb(a)\cdot\hb(b) = a\cdot b + H(b\cdot k)(a\cdot k) + H(a\cdot k)(k\cdot b) + H^2 (a\cdot k)(b\cdot k)\,k^2$, and the last term vanishes; the middle terms add. The inverse case is the same expansion with $H \mapsto -H$, using $\hb^{-1} = 1 - HP_k$ from (1); the sign of the metric correction is the one the paper's definition $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a)\cdot\hb^{-1}(b)$ forces, and at $a = 0$, $H = M/r$, $k = \et - \er$ it reproduces ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein Schwarzschild with the correct mass sign (the metric dual of $\et - \er$ is $dt + dr$, and $\eta - 2H(dt + dr)^2$ is the ingoing form in the advanced time $v = t + r$; the outgoing congruence is $\et + \er$). (3) is (1) and (2) applied to Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-schild-form-kerr-gauge}, plus the comparison with $\hb \;=\; 1 - \beta\,P, \qquad \beta(r) = \sqrt{2M/r}, \qquad P(a) := (a \cdot \et)\,\er$: there $P(a) = (a\cdot\et)\er$ with $\et\cdot\er = 0$ but $\et, \er$ non-null; here the single vector $k$ is null, so the map $P_k$ shears along the very direction it projects onto. The parabolic reading of Remark \claimref{note.interior.parabolic-structural-reason} therefore applies to the whole family with one refinement: rotation moves the gauge trajectory onto the null boundary of the shear cone from the start.

title: Imported: the Kerr curvature
text:
In the conventions of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}, which are the store's curvature sign of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, the curvature operator of the Kerr gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (its field strength, a linear map on physical bivectors) is
\[
\mathcal{R}(B) \;=\; \frac{M}{2}\,\bigl(r - I a\cos\theta\bigr)^{-3}\,\bigl(B + 3\,\sigma_r B\sigma_r\bigr),
\]
where $\sigma_r$ is the unit bivector of the principal planes (the plane pair singled out by the two principal congruences of physically null vectors), $I$ is the pseudoscalar of $\Cl(1,3)$, the inverse cube is taken in the commutative subalgebra $\R \oplus \R I$, and $(r,\theta)$ are oblate spheroidal coordinates on the flat background in which the singular set is the ring $r = 0$, $\theta = \pi/2$, where $\hb$ is undefined (it is unimodular wherever it is defined) and the field strength diverges. \emph{Provenance:} Doran-Lasenby \cite[Ch.~14]{DoranLasenby2003}; the type-D form is classical \cite{Carter1968}.
provenance: C. Doran and A. Lasenby, Geometric Algebra for Physicists, Cambridge University Press (2003)., Ch.~14; B. Carter, Global structure of the Kerr family of gravitational fields, Phys. Rev. 174 (1968), 1559--1571.

title: Complex factorisation and the location of the ring
proof:
(1) $I$ commutes with every even element, in particular with itself and with scalars, so $\R \oplus \R I$ is a commutative subalgebra; $I^2 = -1$ makes $x + Iy \mapsto x + iy$ an algebra isomorphism onto $\C$, under which invertibility is $|z|^2 = z	ilde z = x^2 + y^2 
eq 0$; and inverses computed in $\C$ are inverses in $\Cl(1,3)$ because the subalgebra is unital in the ambient algebra. (2) The shape computation of Proposition \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling} used only $\sigma_r^2 = 1$, the commutation of $I$ with even elements, and the (anti)commutation of the six frame planes with $\sigma_r$; all of it applies verbatim to the principal plane pair of Kerr (\claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature}), with the scalar prefactor now valued in $\R \oplus \R I$. The eigenvalues are $-2\mathfrak M$ on the plane pair and $\mathfrak M$ on the mixed planes, ratio $2 : (-1)$ as before. (3) By (1), $z = r - Ia\cos	heta$ fails to be invertible exactly where $r^2 + a^2\cos^2	heta = 0$, which for real $r$, $	heta$ and $a 
eq 0$ means $r = 0$ and $\cos	heta = 0$ simultaneously: the ring (at $a = 0$ the locus is $\{r = 0\}$, item (4)). On the disc interior $r = 0$, $\cos	heta 
eq 0$, the base is $z = -Ia\cos	heta$ with $z^3 = I\,(a\cos	heta)^3$ and hence $z^{-3} = -I\,(a\cos	heta)^{-3}$, so the scale is $\mathfrak M = -M z^{-3} = M\,I\,(a\cos	heta)^{-3}$ (the script checks the exact value), finite and purely pseudoscalar: the curvature is finite there, and purely dual. (4) Set $a = 0$: $\mathfrak M = -M/r^3$ and $R(B) = -(M/r^3)\,S(B)$, which is Proposition \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling}.

title: Duality winding around the ring
text: The scale $\mathfrak M$ is a complex number attached to each point of the vacuum region, and its phase is a duality angle: multiplication by $I$ on bivector eigenvalues is Hodge duality. Encircle the ring once through the disc into the $r < 0$ sheet of the maximal extension and back (a figure of the original): the base $z = r - Ia\cos\theta$ winds once around $0 \in \C$, so the cubed pole $\mathfrak M \propto z^{-3}$ executes exactly three full duality cycles. The curvature therefore carries a duality-phase monodromy around the codimension-two singular locus, not detectable by any real, metric-level scalar. Two structural consequences are recorded as a conjecture and a pointer. The conjecture:

title: Duality-monodromy fibration over the ring
text: The exceptional structure of the completion over the Kerr ring (the ring of the flat background where the Kerr-Schild gauge field $\hb$ of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, unimodular wherever it is defined, is singular: its potential $H$ diverges) is a duality-monodromy fibration: a bundle of exceptional algebras over the ring in the sense of \cite[Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT4}, refined by codimension two and carrying the monodromy of Remark \claimref{note.interior.duality-winding-around-ring}, whose holonomy connects the sheets of the maximal extension. Equivalently: the codimension-two blow-up that replaces T4's hypersurface wall theory over rotating singularities has structure group containing the duality circle, and the winding number three of the Kerr scale is an invariant of the fibration. \emph{Note.} Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-connection-limit-null-rotation-winding-three} computes the limit of the rotation-gauge field at the ring on the forced cover. The transport holonomy of small loops linking the ring tends to the identity (its clause (6)), so a connection between the sheets is carried by the limiting data, not by transport round the ring: the deck transformation acts by $-1$ on the limit section, which is the adjoint action of the rotor $\hat\varpi\hat z$, the rotation by $\pi$ of the plane transverse to the principal null direction; and at the level of connection values the fibre is the plane $\mathfrak n$ of null rotations about the principal null direction on tangential directions ($\mathfrak n + \R\,F_K \wedge F_N$ with the normal direction), a complex line under the pseudoscalar on which the limit has degree $-3$. The bundle of exceptional algebras in the sense above and its structure group are not addressed there; the conjecture is unchanged. \emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The sheets of the Kerr maximal extension that the holonomy connects are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the ring, the Kerr scale and its winding around the ring are in Gauge Theory Gravity on the invertible region, and the sheets are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.

title: The complex factorisation, and where the ring is
text: The pointer: the singular locus being codimension two rather than a hypersurface confirms that the sheaf-theoretic wall theory of \cite{ButlerT4}, built for hypersurface degeneracy, genuinely needs the geometric blow-up extension for rotating holes; this is a named successor problem (the section ``Scope, and successor problems''), not a gap in the present theorems, whose hypotheses never assume $a = 0$ except where stated.

title: Imported: the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor
text: Every type-D vacuum gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime ($\mathcal{R}(a) = 0$, with Weyl map $\mathcal{W}$ of Petrov type D; Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) admits a valence-two Killing spinor $\chi$ for the covariant derivative $D$, unique up to constant scale, whose square yields a conformal Killing-Yano tensor; for Kerr its scalar invariant is proportional to $r - ia\cos\theta$, and Carter's quartic constant of free-fall motion (worldlines of $D$-parallel velocity, the geodesics of the derived metric) is the associated quadratic first integral; for type-D vacua the Weyl scalar (a component of $\mathcal{W}$ on the bivectors of a principal null tetrad) and the spinor invariant are related by $\Psi_2 \propto \chi^{-3}$, the constant fixed by normalisation. \emph{Provenance:} the Killing spinor and the quadratic integral are Walker-Penrose \cite{WalkerPenrose1970}, the constant of motion Carter \cite{Carter1968}; the $\Psi_2 \propto \chi^{-3}$ relation is the standard type-$\{22\}$ statement descending from \cite{WalkerPenrose1970}, and for Kerr the corresponding statement about the framework's own scale $\mathfrak M$ is derived in Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor} from Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature} and the Killing-spinor scalar above, with no appeal to this clause and none to the imported normalisation; the script checks that derivation.
provenance: M. Walker and R. Penrose, On quadratic first integrals of the geodesic equations for type $22$ spacetimes, Commun. Math. Phys. 18 (1970), 265--274.; B. Carter, Global structure of the Kerr family of gravitational fields, Phys. Rev. 174 (1968), 1559--1571.

title: The complex scale is the inverse cube of the Killing spinor
text:
Identify the commutative subalgebra $\R \oplus \R I$ with $\C$ as in Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring}(1), matching $I$ with $i$ (an orientation choice, fixed once). Then the Kerr curvature scale of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature} is
\[
\mathfrak M \;=\; -M\,\chi^{-3}
\]
with $\chi = r - Ia\cos\theta$ the Killing-spinor scale of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-walker-penrose-killing-spinor} in the same normalisation. Consequently: the framework's ``scalar-plus-pseudoscalar scale'', discovered in Proposition \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling} as the carrier of the entire approach to the singularity and complexified by rotation in Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring}, is a hidden spinor object, a Killing spinor (a solution of Penrose's twistor equation): the very spinor that generates Carter's constant and the hidden symmetries of the Kerr interior. And the duality monodromy of Remark \claimref{note.interior.duality-winding-around-ring} is $-3$ times (thrice, in the opposite sense) the winding of the Killing spinor around the ring.
proof: The content is an identification, and the proof is the comparison of the two displayed objects in one convention. By Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature} and Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring} the scale is $\mathfrak M = -M(r - Ia\cos\theta)^{-3}$; by Fact \claimref{interior.imported-walker-penrose-killing-spinor} the Killing-spinor scalar is $c\,(r - ia\cos\theta)$ for a nonzero constant $c$ fixed by normalising the spinor; choosing the normalisation $c = 1$ (which the constant-scale freedom of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-walker-penrose-killing-spinor} permits) and matching $I \leftrightarrow i$ gives $\mathfrak M = -M\chi^{-3}$ exactly. What is \emph{not} conventional, and carries the content: (a) the power is three, so the winding statement of Remark \claimref{note.interior.duality-winding-around-ring} is winding number three of $\chi$ itself; (b) the object on the left is constructed from curvature and the transport framework's invertibility criterion alone, with no reference to spinors, geodesics, or separability, while the object on the right generates Carter's constant; their identification is a nontrivial fact about where the framework's scale lies. The $\Psi_2 \propto \chi^{-3}$ clause of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-walker-penrose-killing-spinor} is the spinor-calculus instance of this computation rather than an input to it: nothing above uses it, the derivation running on Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature} and the Killing-spinor scalar alone, and $\mathfrak M$ is the type-D curvature scale that $\Psi_2$ names in the spinor conventions, equal to it up to the constant fixed by Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}.

title: Points of contact with established physics, kept in view
text: As the series' practice requires, the points of contact are stated where they occur. The principal plane pair of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature} is the eigenplane structure of a type-D Weyl operator (Petrov); the Killing spinor is the standard generator of Kerr's hidden symmetry (Carter's constant, symmetry operators for wave equations); and the identification of Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor} places the framework's conformal scale inside Penrose's twistor theory, which in geometric algebra is the theory of the conformal spinor space $\CS$ of $\Cl(2,4)$; its systematic development for the series (ascended spinors, incidence, the palatial bridge) belongs to the correspondence paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9}. Nothing in Parts one and two depended on these identifications; Part three's point is that the framework's internal objects coincide with them exactly.

title: The perturbed Cauchy horizon
text: Exact Kerr was never the hard part of the test. Since Kerr is Ricci-flat, Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations} applies verbatim on the whole vacuum region, inner horizons included: the parallel null tractor exists globally, and exact Kerr passes the covariance test outright. The physical question is what survives perturbation, because the Cauchy horizon is known to be unstable. The established results are imported with provenance and then read.

title: Imported: mass inflation and $C^0$ stability
text: (i) Infalling radiation is blueshifted without bound at the Kerr Cauchy horizon, generically driving unbounded growth of the quasi-local (Hawking) mass: mass inflation. (ii) For dynamical vacuum perturbations of Kerr initial data, the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) extends continuously ($C^0$) across the Cauchy horizon. (ii$'$) In spherical symmetry (the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field system with two-ended asymptotically flat data), the derived metric extends continuously across the Cauchy horizon while, generically, its Christoffel symbols (the components of the connection, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii)) fail to be locally square-integrable: a weak null singularity. The same generic failure, with blow-up of the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B)$, is the expected picture for the Kerr perturbations of (ii); it is stated there as a conjecture and is not proved. (iii) Tidal deformations of infalling observers remain finite through the weak null singularity. \emph{Provenance:} (i) Poisson-Israel \cite{PoissonIsrael1990}; (ii) Dafermos-Luk \cite{DafermosLuk2017}; (ii$'$) Luk-Oh \cite{LukOh2019a,LukOh2019b}; (iii) Ori \cite{Ori1991}. \emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The Cauchy horizon, as the boundary of the maximal development of two-ended data, and the extension of the field across it are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region (the blueshift and mass growth, and the regularity classes of the field and its connection along the approach) are in Gauge Theory Gravity, and the Cauchy horizon and the extension across it are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
provenance: E. Poisson and W. Israel, Internal structure of black holes, Phys. Rev. D 41 (1990), 1796--1809.; M. Dafermos and J. Luk, The interior of dynamical vacuum black holes I: the $C^0$-stability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon, preprint, arXiv:1710.01722 (2017).; J. Luk and S.-J. Oh, Strong cosmic censorship in spherical symmetry for two-ended asymptotically flat initial data I. The interior of the black hole region, Ann. of Math. (2) 190 (2019), 1--111.; J. Luk and S.-J. Oh, Strong cosmic censorship in spherical symmetry for two-ended asymptotically flat initial data II. The exterior of the black hole region, Ann. PDE 5 (2019), Art. 6.; A. Ori, Inner structure of a charged black hole: an exact mass-inflation solution, Phys. Rev. Lett. 67 (1991), 789--792.

title: The filtration at the Cauchy horizon, read from the literature
text:
In the framework's language, Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability} yields three findings; each is a reading of the imported statements, and the one-step translation carrying each reading is proved below.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Obstruction type:} the degeneration at the perturbed Cauchy horizon is of type N (null kernel direction), in the degenerate-radical reading the series fixes at the Schwarzschild centre \cite[Prop.~3.1]{ButlerT5}, which extends T1's taxonomy \cite[Def.~3.1]{ButlerT1} to radical directions through \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5]{ButlerT4}: the same class as at the centre, realised on a null hypersurface rather than at a point.
\item \emph{Filtration by derivative level:} a $C^0$ derived metric $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) determines a $C^0$ conformal class (pointwise multiplication by a positive function preserves continuity, and the class map $g \mapsto [g]$ is continuous), so point-level structure, metric and conformal alike, extends continuously across the Cauchy horizon, while connection-level structure, the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ (whose reading on $g$ is the Levi-Civita connection) and the tractor connection alike (on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, whose $\nO$ summand carries the Schouten map, two derivatives of $g$), generically fails: proved in spherical symmetry by Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}(ii$'$), expected for Kerr. The ordering is by derivative level; a strict separation of the conformal description from the metric one at fixed derivative level is not among the imports, and is exactly the open transport question of the section ``Scope, and successor problems''.
\item \emph{Filtration:} in a physical frame adapted to the horizon generators, the divergent components of the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B)$ are those of extreme boost weight, the top of the parabolic filtration attached to the null direction: the divergence occupies the nilpotent slots, as in every previous instance of the obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The Cauchy horizon, as the boundary of the maximal development, and the extension of the field across it are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region (the type and kernel of the degeneration, the regularity of the derived metric and of $\Omega$ along the approach, the boost weights of the divergent components) are in Gauge Theory Gravity, and the Cauchy horizon and the extension across it are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
proof: The proof speaks of the derived metric $g$ of the gravitational field and of its Levi-Civita connection, which Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i) and (ii) read as $\hb$ and the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ on flat spacetime. (1) The degenerating direction is the null generator of the Cauchy horizon; the kernel of the degenerating metric data is spanned by a null vector, the type-N condition in the degenerate-radical reading imported above (T1's Definition 3.1 is stated for nondegenerate algebras; the extension to radical directions is T4's, routed as at the Schwarzschild centre through \cite[Prop.~3.1]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.type-n-only-type-n})). (2) The mathematical content is elementary and proved here: if $g_n \to g$ in $C^0$ with $g$ a continuous nondegenerate metric, then for any continuous positive $\omega$, $\omega g_n \to \omega g$ in $C^0$, so the conformal class of the $C^0$ extension is a $C^0$-extended conformal class; Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}(ii) supplies the $C^0$ metric extension for Kerr perturbations, and Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}(ii$'$) the generic failure at one derivative, proved in spherical symmetry and expected for Kerr. At connection level the two descriptions succeed or fail together: the tractor connection \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection} carries the Levi-Civita action and the Schouten tensor, first and second derivatives of $g$, so the generic failure of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}(ii$'$) reaches it exactly where it reaches the metric connection; no separation between the descriptions is claimed, or available, from the imports. (3) is the boost-weight structure of weak null singularities as established in the works cited in Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}: the blow-up is in the transversal derivative components, which carry extreme weight under the boost fixing the horizon generator; we import the analytic statement and observe only that extreme boost weight is precisely the nilradical slot of the parabolic fixing the null direction (Proposition \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model}(3)).

title: The conclusion, and two cautions
text: Proposition \claimref{interior.filtration-cauchy-horizon-read-literature}(2) is a filtration statement, and it is read as exactly that: survival at the perturbed Cauchy horizon is ordered by derivative level, with the divergence in the nilpotent slots, which is the structure the framework predicts. What the literature does not supply is a strict separation of the conformal from the metric description at fixed derivative level: the framework's central claim, that the ascended description persists where the metric one fails, therefore rests at the Cauchy horizon on the open transport question of successor problem (1), not on a finished theorem. The Kerr test is passed at the level the imports reach, and no further. Two cautions make the conclusion more precise, both recorded as scope. First, generic perturbations destroy type-D rigidity: the exact shape factorisations of Propositions \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling} and \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring} are properties of the exact family, and robust statements off it must be made at the level of the boost-weight filtration rather than the fixed operator $S$. Second, what the framework most needs, a quantitative transport theorem (convergence of tractor parallel transport along causal curves crossing the Cauchy horizon), needs integrability of the connection along such curves: a property strictly between the established $C^0$ metric extension and the $C^1$ statement whose generic failure is proved in spherical symmetry and expected for Kerr, and not currently available in either direction. It is the sharpest open problem the test leaves, and it is registered in the section ``Scope, and successor problems''.

title: What is proved, what is imported, what is conjectured
text:
\emph{Proved in this paper, at the standard of \cite{ButlerT1}:} the unipotent-ray proposition and the exact scale decoupling (Propositions \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}, \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling}); the elementary tractor lemmas and the entire flat-model dictionary (Lemma \claimref{interior.metric-parallelism-trace-schouten-condition}, Propositions \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model}, \claimref{interior.non-null-stabilisers-section-they-act}); the vacuum theorem, the $\Lambda$ theorem with its internal sign-fixing, and the stabiliser rotation (Theorems \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}, \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, Lemma \claimref{interior.sign-fixed-internally}, Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}); the Kasner lemmas with explicit rates (Lemmas \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}, \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}, \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly}); the boost-generation lemma (Lemma \claimref{interior.boosts-generate-exactly-levi-factor}); the weighted limit theorem and its Schwarzschild-de Sitter extension (Theorems \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}, \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}), with the boundary holonomy algebra in the values-level sense fixed by Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}; the transport-level convergence theorem along tangential curves for the whole admissible class and its Schwarzschild $\varphi$-line corollary with rate (Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves}, Corollary \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-lines-exactly}); the Kerr-Schild unipotency and complex-factorisation propositions (Propositions \claimref{interior.unipotency-across-kerr-family}, \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring}); and the elementary halves of Propositions \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor} and \claimref{interior.filtration-cauchy-horizon-read-literature}.

\emph{Imported as Facts with provenance:} the GTG-Einstein equivalence and the two curvature computations (Facts \claimref{interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}, \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}, \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-curvature}); the tractor connection (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection}); the Kerr-Schild form (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-schild-form-kerr-gauge}); the Walker-Penrose spinor (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-walker-penrose-killing-spinor}); the Cauchy-horizon results (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}). Each is used only through its stated content.

\emph{Scoped and open:} the weighted limit theorem's scope is the admissible (Einstein velocity-dominated) class of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}, with the mixmaster delimiter of Remark \claimref{note.interior.generic-delimiter-mixmaster} marking the provable boundary; the duality-monodromy conjecture (Conjecture \claimref{interior.duality-monodromy-fibration-over-ring}) is posed, not proved; and the limits of the Kerr conclusion are itemised in Remark \claimref{note.interior.conclusion-two-cautions}.

title: Successor problems
text: Five problems are named for the series' open directions, in decreasing order of urgency for the programme. (1) \emph{The quantitative transport theorem at the Cauchy horizon:} establish or refute integrability of the tractor connection along causal curves crossing the perturbed Cauchy horizon; either outcome sharpens Proposition \claimref{interior.filtration-cauchy-horizon-read-literature} into a statement about the completion itself. (2) \emph{The billiard-invariant weighted limit:} formulate and prove the analogue of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} on the quotient by Kasner-axis dynamics, where the generic mixmaster approach lies; the admissibility integral of Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} says exactly what fails framewise. (3) \emph{The ring blow-up:} extend the wall theory of \cite{ButlerT4} to codimension two and prove or refute Conjecture \claimref{interior.duality-monodromy-fibration-over-ring}; the winding number three of Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor} is the first invariant any such theory must reproduce. (4) \emph{Edge regularity in general:} for a general admissible metric, control the tangential derivatives of the error $E_{\tau}$ on compact sets of the exceptional set, which admissibility does not include; this is the only analysis left in the edge problem, since the transport-level comparison along all tangential curves of fixed Hubble-normalised length is Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} for the whole admissible class and the tangential regularity holds at Schwarzschild by symmetry (Corollary \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-lines-exactly}). (5) \emph{Carter's constant inside GTG:} derive the quadratic first integral directly from the scale identification of Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor} within the gauge-theoretic formalism, completing the connection the identification begins. The weighted completion of the wall program in its generic-singularity extension depends on (2) and on (4); the density constant $\nu$ of the entropy paper is stated for Schwarzschild, inside the admissible class with constant exponents and no bounces, where (2) does not arise and (4) is closed, so what that prediction still waits on is the calibration of the count, not analysis here.

title: Position in the series
text: This paper is T6 of the series. It consumes four predecessors. From the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} it takes the working language of geometric algebra; from the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} the zero-divisor taxonomy, the no-go theorem whose transvections reappear here as the nilradical of the frozen point's stabiliser, and the completion that fixes the ambient algebra $\Cl(2,4)$; from the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} the wall-level theory of degeneration whose codimension-two extension Conjecture \claimref{interior.duality-monodromy-fibration-over-ring} names; and from the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} the curvature computation imported as Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum} and the six-step chain whose three geometric links this paper closes. It supplies, downstream: the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} imports the GTG equivalence and the vacuum theorem (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}, Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}); the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} builds on the Kasner form of the interior (Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}), the weighted-limit results of the section ``Part three, first half: the approach'', and the duality-monodromy conjecture (Conjecture \claimref{interior.duality-monodromy-fibration-over-ring}); the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} develops the flat-model dictionary of the section ``Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point'', the vacuum and $\Lambda$ theorems, and the Killing-spinor identification (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor}); and the dark-energy paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} takes the frozen point, its norm $\Lambda/3$, and the parabolic-to-reductive stabiliser rotation (Theorems \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}, \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}) as its kinematic base.

title: The degeneration, exactly
text:
As $r \to 0$, exactly and with every identity holding at finite $\beta$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (The map.) $\beta^{-1}\hb = \beta^{-1}\,\mathrm{id} - P$, so $\beta^{-1}\hb \to -P$: a rank-one map with image $\R\,\er$ and kernel $\et^{\perp} = \operatorname{span}(\er, e_\vartheta, e_\varphi)$.
\item (The metric.) $\beta^{-2} g(a,b) = -(a\cdot\et)(b\cdot\et) + \beta^{-1}\bigl[(a\cdot\et)(b\cdot\er) + (b\cdot\et)(a\cdot\er)\bigr] + \beta^{-2}(a \cdot b)$, so $\beta^{-2}g \to \hat g$ with
\[
\hat g(a,b) \;=\; -(a\cdot\et)(b\cdot\et) :
\]
a form of rank one and signature $(0,1,3)$, whose radical is $\et^{\perp}$, the kernel of the limit map.
\item (The null direction, located.) The folded direction $\er$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.cones-fold} lies in the radical of $\hat g$ and is $\hat g$-null, while $g(\er,\er) = -1$ at every finite radius: the nullity of the degenerate direction is a property of the limit form, not of the flat background, and this is the exact content of the phrase ``degeneration through a null kernel direction''. It is the datum Step 2 uses.
\end{enumerate}

title: Non-removability: the invariant argument
text:
The curvature scalar
\[
K \;:=\; R_{abcd}R^{abcd} \;=\; 4\Bigl(2\,\bigl(\tfrac{2M}{r^3}\bigr)^2 + 4\,\bigl(\tfrac{M}{r^3}\bigr)^2\Bigr) \;=\; \frac{48\,M^2}{r^6}
\;\longrightarrow\; \infty \quad (r \to 0),
\]
and $K$ is invariant under every gauge transformation of the theory, $r$-dependent transformations of arbitrary size included. Hence no gauge choice removes the degeneration at $r = 0$: the division-by-zero locus is a property of the solution, not of its presentation.

title: The solution, and where the divergence lies
text:
The pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ of $\hb(a) \;=\; a - \beta\,(a \cdot \et)\,\er \;=\; (1 - \beta P)(a), \qquad \beta(r) = \sqrt{2M/r}, \qquad P(a) := (a \cdot \et)\,\er$ and Proposition \claimref{singularity.connection-bivector-computed} solves the vacuum field equations $\mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac12\, a\, \mathcal{R} \;=\; 8\pi\, T(a), \qquad D \wedge \hb(a) \;=\; \hb(\nabla \wedge a)$ at every $r > 0$, and the divergence of the classical description resides in $\Omega$ and in the curvature, not in $\hb$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (The radial curvature, from the gauge field alone.) On the radial plane both connection values are multiples of the single bivector $\sigma_r$, so the commutator term of the field strength the relation displayed with \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} vanishes identically and nothing depends on $t$; hence, in two lines,
\[
\mathcal{R}(\partial_t \wedge \partial_r)
\;=\; \partial_t\,\Omega(\partial_r) - \partial_r\,\Omega(\partial_t) + \Omega(\partial_t)\times\Omega(\partial_r)
\;=\; -\,\partial_r\Bigl(\frac{M}{r^2}\Bigr)\sigma_r
\;=\; \frac{2M}{r^3}\,\sigma_r :
\]
the radial plane is an eigenplane of the curvature with eigenvalue of magnitude $2M/r^3$, derived without leaving the gauge formalism.
\item (Vacuum.) The full curvature operator is diagonal on the six frame planes with eigenvalues of magnitudes $(2M/r^3, M/r^3, M/r^3, M/r^3, M/r^3, 2M/r^3)$ and vanishing Ricci contraction: the mixed and angular planes are computed in the section ``The curvature operator, by the Cartan structure equations'' in the static chart, where the computation is shortest, and the two pictures agree on the invertible region by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}. The shape this spectrum assembles into is Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}'s task.
\item (Unimodularity.) $\det \hb = 1$ exactly, at every radius, horizon included: $P$ is rank-one nilpotent, so $1 - \beta P$ is unipotent as a matrix. Likewise the $(t,r)$ block of the metric $g(a,b) \;=\; \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ has determinant $-1$ at every radius. Nothing determinant-like degenerates at any $r > 0$: at finite radius the classical field is a volume-preserving shear, and the entire divergence of the approach is carried by the connection (Proposition \claimref{singularity.connection-bivector-computed}(3)) and by the curvature, both of which diverge, and by the metric components themselves, which diverge without a rescaled limit unless one is taken exactly as in Proposition \claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly}.
\end{enumerate}

title: Type N, and only type N
text: The obstruction at $r = 0$ is type N in the taxonomy of \cite[\S 3]{ButlerT1}: an isotropic direction without a metric partner, in the degenerate sense in which the root paper hands such cases to the sheaf paper. Type C cannot occur: $\Cl(1,3)$ has $p - q = -2 \equiv 6 \pmod 8$, hence is central simple ($\cong \Mat_2(\HH)$), has no central idempotents, and offers ideal fusion nothing to fuse. Type P, which is present in $\Cl(1,3)$ as in every algebra of its size, demands no transport: its rule is the rule of no rule \cite[\S 6, Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT1}, so it neither licenses nor obstructs the ascent. The operative transport rule is Rule 1, the Witt completion, and by \cite[Thm.~3.6]{ButlerT3} no floor of the resulting tower ever develops a type-C obstruction either. This is the algorithm's Step 2 \cite[\S 8.1, Step 2]{ButlerT1}, with both diagnostic questions answered by computation.

title: Bivectors form the Lie algebra of the orthogonal group
Orthogonal vectors anticommute
text: For $u, v \in V$: $u v = -v u$ if and only if $B(u, v) = 0$. In an orthogonal basis $e_1, \dots, e_n$, $e_i e_j = -e_j e_i$ for $i \ne j$ and $e_i^{2} = Q(e_i)$, and the product of two basis blades is $e_I e_J = \pm \bigl(\prod_{i \in I \cap J} Q(e_i)\bigr)\, e_{I \triangle J}$, the sign being $(-1)$ to the number of pairs $(i, j) \in I \times J$ with $i > j$.

title: Orthogonal bases and the law of inertia
text: Every real quadratic space $(V, Q)$ of dimension $n$ has an orthogonal basis $e_1, \dots, e_n$ with $Q(e_i) \in \{1, -1, 0\}$. The numbers $p$, $q$ and $r$ of basis vectors with $Q(e_i) = 1$, $-1$ and $0$ do not depend on the basis (Sylvester's law of inertia). Moreover $r = \dim \operatorname{rad} V$, and $p + q$ is the rank of any Gram matrix of $B$. Two real quadratic spaces are isometric if and only if they have the same $(p, q, r)$.
provenance: T. Y. Lam, Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields, AMS (2005)., the diagonalisation of forms and Sylvester's law of inertia (real case)

title: The no-echo prediction, registered
text: The framework's quantum structure lies at the stretched singularity, $r_c = (2M)^{1/3}$ in Planck units, by Postulate \claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff} (C1): deep inside the hole, at Planck curvature, and nowhere near the horizon, which remains exactly the smooth vacuum horizon of classical general relativity (the exterior dictionary is exact, \cite[Fact 2.1]{ButlerT6}). The registered prediction: post-merger ringdown is the Kerr quasinormal spectrum of general relativity with \emph{no} modification, and in particular no echo train at the Planck-structure delay $\tau_{\mathrm{echo}} \approx 8M\ln(M/m_P)$ (the delay at which near-horizon structure at Planck distance would reflect \cite{CardosoPani2017}), of order tens to hundreds of milliseconds for stellar-mass remnants ($35$ ms at $10\,M_\odot$, $0.1$ to $0.25$ s for remnants of $30$ to $70\,M_\odot$): within the sensitivity band of existing detectors. A single statistically confirmed echo train would refute the framework's localisation of quantum structure. The prediction is stated so that it can fail.
